title: Unified Retail Inventory Analytics
business: Retail organizations managing massive, disparate supply chain datasets.
problem: Data silos between warehouse management systems and point-of-sale logs prevent real-time inventory visibility, leading to stockouts.
solution: Azure Databricks provides an integrated Apache Spark-based lakehouse platform to unify batch and streaming data into a single source of truth for analytics.
steps: Provision an Azure Databricks workspace within the existing Azure tenant.
Configure data ingestion pipelines to pull raw logs from warehouse and POS systems into the lakehouse.
Execute Spark-based transformation jobs to normalize and join disparate datasets.
Expose the refined data layer for downstream business intelligence reporting.
outcome: Improved inventory accuracy and reduced stockout incidents through a unified, high-performance data foundation.
limitation: The platform requires significant cluster management and configuration to optimize resource utilization; verify this by monitoring job execution times and cluster idle metrics.

diagram.title: Retail Data Lakehouse Flow
diagram.description: Data flows from source systems through the Databricks processing layer to the final analytics output.

code.content:
# Read raw data from storage
df = spark.read.format('delta').load('/mnt/raw_inventory')
# Perform transformation to unify schemas
refined_df = df.filter(df.status == 'active')
# Write to the lakehouse
refined_df.write.format('delta').save('/mnt/lakehouse/inventory')
code.explanation: This snippet demonstrates reading raw inventory data, filtering for active items, and saving the result into the Delta Lake format within the Azure Databricks environment.
